title: fix: prevent false task completion cascade (t163)
body:
## Summary

Adds 4 layers of protection against false task completions that cascade into auto-closed GitHub issues:

1. **AGENTS.md rules** (t163.1): Documents that tasks must NEVER be marked `[x]` without a merged PR containing real deliverables
2. **issue-sync guard** (t163.2): `cmd_close()` now requires a merged PR or `verified:YYYY-MM-DD` field before closing issues. `--force` flag available for override
3. **pre-commit warning** (t163.3): Warns when TODO.md tasks transition `[ ]` -> `[x]` without evidence of a merged PR
4. **supervisor verify** (t163.4): `verify_task_deliverables()` checks PR is merged with substantive file changes before `update_todo_on_complete()` marks `[x]`

## Root Cause

The supervisor marked tasks "deployed" in its DB after running the post-PR lifecycle, then `update_todo_on_complete()` blindly marked `[x]` in TODO.md. The `issue-sync` GitHub Action then auto-closed 38 issues. Many of those tasks had `no_pr` or `task_only` status — meaning no real work was done.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/AGENTS.md` | Task completion rules in Planning & Tasks section |
| `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` | `task_has_completion_evidence()` + guard in `cmd_close()` + `--force` flag |
| `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` | `validate_todo_completions()` check for `[ ]` -> `[x]` transitions |
| `.agents/scripts/supervisor-helper.sh` | `verify_task_deliverables()` + guard in `update_todo_on_complete()` |

## Testing

title: fix: seed evaluate_worker PR URL from DB to prevent clean_exit_no_signal retry loop
body:
## Summary

- **Bug**: Workers that create a PR and exit 0 without emitting `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` were incorrectly retried as `clean_exit_no_signal` because the `gh pr list` fallback in `evaluate_worker()` could fail (worktree cleaned up, network issues, branch name mismatch)
- **Fix**: `evaluate_worker()` now checks the `tasks.pr_url` DB column first (populated by `check_pr_status()` in prior pulse cycles) before falling back to expensive `gh pr list` API calls
- **Bonus**: `TASK_COMPLETE` outcomes now include the PR URL when available instead of always returning `task_only`

## Changes

**`.agents/scripts/supervisor-helper.sh`** (`evaluate_worker()`):
1. Added `pr_url` to the DB query (`SELECT ... pr_url FROM tasks`)
2. Added DB seed step: if `meta_pr_url` is empty but `tasks.pr_url` has a valid URL, use it
3. Updated `TASK_COMPLETE` handler to include PR URL when available
4. Updated `clean_exit_no_signal` comment to document the three-source PR detection (DB seed t171, gh fallback t161, log metadata)

## Root Cause

The evaluation flow had a gap between PR detection sources:
- Log metadata: always empty (disabled in t151 to prevent false positives)
- `gh pr list` fallback: unreliable (requires valid worktree path, network, correct branch name)
- DB `pr_url` column: **not checked** (populated by `check_pr_status()` in prior pulse cycles)

This meant workers that completed successfully could be retried 3 times before exhausting retries, wasting compute and delaying task completion.

Closes #580

title: fix: resolve supervisor concurrency limiter race condition (t172)
body:
## Summary

Fixes GH#578 — TOCTOU race condition in supervisor concurrency limiter.

**Root Cause**: `cmd_next()` checked running count and computed available slots, then `cmd_dispatch()` checked again independently. Between these checks (during the same pulse loop), prior dispatches in the loop incremented the running count, but `cmd_next()` had already returned tasks based on the stale count.

**Fix**:
- Removed concurrency check from `cmd_next()` — it now returns queued tasks without slot checking
- `cmd_dispatch()` is the single authoritative concurrency gate with a fresh running count at dispatch time
- Added TOCTOU documentation to `cmd_next()` explaining the design decision
- Added 82-line test for the concurrency race condition

Closes #578

title: hotfix: fix dispatch command breaking on multi-line prompts
body:
## Summary

- Fixes supervisor worker dispatch failing silently when prompts contain newlines (from t173 worker restrictions)
- Workers were receiving malformed commands and printing help text instead of executing tasks
- Root cause: `printf '%q'` produces `$'\n'` sequences that break inside `bash -c` double-quoted strings

## Root Cause

`build_dispatch_cmd()` correctly builds multi-line prompts (task description + worker restrictions + memory context). But `cmd_dispatch()` embeds the escaped command in a `bash -c` string:

```bash
nohup bash -c "... && $(printf '%q ' "${cmd_parts[@]}") > ..." &
```

The `$'\n'` from `printf '%q'` gets split across lines inside the double-quoted `bash -c` argument, producing invalid syntax. The worker process receives a truncated/malformed command and exits immediately with the help text.

## Fix

Write dispatch commands to temp script files (`pids/{task_id}-dispatch.sh`) and execute those instead. The `printf '%q'` output is valid bash when written to its own file — the `$'\n'` sequences are interpreted correctly by the script's own bash process.

Applied to both `cmd_dispatch` (tabby + headless paths) and `cmd_reprompt`.

## Impact

- **All supervisor-dispatched workers since PR #649 (t173)** were affected — the multi-line worker restriction text was added in that PR
- This explains why t175 and t176 immediately failed with `ambiguous_skipped_ai` (EXIT:1, 28-line logs containing only help text)
- The batch `self-improvement-02` will work after this fix is deployed

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations
- All 78 supervisor state machine tests pass (77 passed, 1 skipped)
- Verified generated dispatch script is syntactically valid (`bash -n` passes)
- Verified `$'\n'` sequences are correctly interpreted in standalone script files

title: hotfix: use NUL-delimited IPC for dispatch command builder
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the root cause of all supervisor-dispatched workers failing since PR #649 (t173 worker restrictions)
- Multi-line prompts were being split into separate positional arguments instead of staying as one argument
- Workers received malformed commands and exited immediately with help text (EXIT:1)

## Root Cause (deeper than #653)

PR #653 fixed the `bash -c` quoting issue but missed the upstream problem: `build_dispatch_cmd()` outputs arguments via `echo` (newline-delimited), and `cmd_dispatch()` reads them with `while IFS= read -r`. When the prompt contains newlines (from worker restrictions, memory context), `read -r` splits the single prompt argument into multiple array elements.

Example: a prompt like:
```
/full-loop t175 --headless -- Fix bug

## MANDATORY Worker Restrictions
- Do NOT edit TODO.md
```

Was being split into 4 separate arguments instead of 1, causing `opencode run` to misparse the command.

## Fix

- `build_dispatch_cmd()`: Replace `echo` with `printf '%s\0'` (NUL-delimited output)

title: feat: add uncertainty decision framework for headless workers (t176)
body:
## Summary

- Adds a structured decision framework for headless workers to determine when to make autonomous decisions vs flag uncertainty and exit cleanly
- Injects the framework directly into every supervisor-dispatched worker prompt via `build_dispatch_cmd()` in supervisor-helper.sh
- Documents the full framework with decision tree, proceed/exit tables, examples, and supervisor integration in headless-dispatch.md
- Adds rule 7 to the full-loop.md headless dispatch rules with concrete proceed/exit criteria

## Problem

Workers previously had only a vague instruction: "If you encounter ambiguity, make a reasonable decision and document it in a commit message. If truly blocked, exit cleanly." This led to:
- Workers making risky autonomous decisions that should have been flagged
- Workers exiting on trivial ambiguities that they could have resolved themselves
- Wasted retries and compute from unclear exit behavior

## Solution

A three-question decision tree:
1. Can I infer intent from context + codebase conventions? → Proceed
2. Would getting this wrong cause irreversible damage? → Exit
3. Does this affect only my task scope? → Proceed if yes, exit if no

With specific examples for both categories (proceed: style choices, vague descriptions, equivalent patterns; exit: contradictions, breaking API changes, missing credentials, architectural decisions).

title: fix: handle missing worktrees in cmd_reprompt between retries (t178)
body:
## Summary

- Fix variable ordering bug where `needs_fresh_worktree` was referenced before declaration, causing clean-slate retry prompts to never trigger
- Add missing worktree detection and recreation when the worktree directory disappears between retries (manual cleanup, `wt prune`, disk cleanup, etc.)
- Ensure workers get the correct "start fresh" prompt when a worktree is recreated, instead of being told to continue from a non-existent previous attempt

## Details

`cmd_reprompt` had three related bugs:

1. **Variable ordering**: `needs_fresh_worktree` was checked at line 3819 in prompt construction but not declared until line 3841. In bash, this means the check always evaluated to false, so the clean-slate prompt was dead code.

2. **Missing worktree fallback**: When `tworktree` was set in the DB but the directory no longer existed, the code fell back to `work_dir="$trepo"` (the main repo). Workers would then run in the main repo instead of a proper worktree.

3. **Prompt mismatch**: Even if the worktree was recreated, the prompt still told the worker to "continue where the previous attempt left off" — which makes no sense for a fresh worktree.

The fix restructures `cmd_reprompt` to:
1. Detect and handle worktree state (clean-slate + missing) **before** building the prompt message
2. Recreate missing worktrees using `create_task_worktree` (same pattern as the review-fix code at line 4209)
3. Set `needs_fresh_worktree=true` when a worktree is recreated so the prompt correctly instructs the worker to start fresh

## Testing

- All 77 supervisor state machine tests pass
- All 55/56 batch quality hardening tests pass (1 expected diff: deployed vs repo)
- Zero new ShellCheck violations

title: fix: check for open PRs before deleting 'stale' branches in worktree cleanup
body:
## Summary

- Prevents data loss when `create_task_worktree()` deletes branches that have open PRs with unmerged work
- Adds `gh pr list --head` check before marking branches as stale in both worktree-exists and branch-only code paths

## Root Cause

`create_task_worktree()` treated branches with 0 commits ahead of main as "stale" and deleted them. But with squash merges, a branch can show 0 commits ahead while still having an open PR with unmerged work — e.g., after the remote branch was pruned during cleanup and recreated via rebase.

**Incident**: t133's worker created PR #661 with valid changes. During a retry, `create_task_worktree()` saw the branch had 0 commits ahead (after rebase) and deleted it. The open PR became unmergeable and the worker's commit was lost.

## Fix

Before marking a branch as stale (in both the worktree-exists and branch-only paths), query GitHub:

```bash
gh pr list --head "$branch_name" --state open --json number --jq 'length'
```

If an open PR exists, skip cleanup and preserve the branch.

## Self-Learning

- Stored `FAILED_APPROACH` memory: stale branch cleanup can delete branches with open PRs
- This fix prevents the same data loss pattern in future batches

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations
- All 78 supervisor state machine tests pass

## Summary

- Diagnostic tasks (`diagnostic_of IS NOT NULL`) become stale when their parent task reaches a terminal state (`deployed`/`cancelled`/`failed`/`complete`/`merged`) before the diagnostic is dispatched

title: fix: improve supervisor dispatch error capture when worker fails to start (t183)
body:
## Summary

- **Pre-create log files** with dispatch metadata before spawning workers — eliminates `no_log_file` failures by ensuring diagnostic context exists even when workers fail to start
- **Add `WORKER_STARTED` sentinel** to all dispatch scripts — enables distinguishing "worker never started" from "worker started but produced no output"
- **Replace `nohup bash -c ... &>/dev/null`** with wrapper scripts that capture stderr from dispatch scripts — previously all startup errors were silently swallowed
- **Enhanced `evaluate_worker()` diagnostics** — granular failure types (`no_log_path_in_db`, `log_file_missing`, `log_file_empty`, `worker_never_started:WORKER_DISPATCH_ERROR:...`) replace the opaque `no_log_file`
- **Enable self-healing for dispatch failures** — removed `no_log_file` from `is_self_heal_eligible()` exclusion list since diagnostic metadata is now available
- **Add `worker_started` and `dispatch_error` fields** to `extract_log_metadata()` for structured outcome analysis

## Problem

When a supervisor-dispatched worker failed to start (e.g., `opencode` not found, permission error, worktree path invalid), the evaluation returned `failed:no_log_file` with zero diagnostic context. This was a dead end:
- No way to distinguish between different failure modes
- Self-healing was explicitly disabled for `no_log_file` failures
- The `nohup bash -c '...' &>/dev/null` pattern swallowed all stderr from the dispatch process
- Log files were only created by shell redirection (`> log_file`), so if the shell command itself failed, no log was created

## Solution

Applied consistently across all 3 dispatch sites (`cmd_dispatch`, `cmd_reprompt`, review-fix dispatch):

1. **Pre-create log file** with metadata header before spawning the worker
2. **Startup sentinel** (`WORKER_STARTED`) emitted by dispatch script on successful start
3. **Wrapper script** pattern replaces inline `bash -c` — captures all errors into the log file
4. **Granular evaluation** checks log existence, emptiness, sentinel presence, and extracts specific error messages

## Testing

- Bash syntax validation: PASS
- ShellCheck: No new warnings (pre-existing SC2034 only)
- Existing state machine tests: All passing tests still pass
- 6 new smoke tests covering all diagnostic paths:
  - No log path in DB → `failed:no_log_path_in_db`
  - Missing log file → `failed:log_file_missing:no_dispatch_scripts:no_pid_file`
  - Empty log file → `failed:log_file_empty`
  - Metadata only (no sentinel) → `failed:worker_never_started:no_sentinel`
  - Normal completion → `complete:no_pr` (unchanged)
  - Dispatch error → `failed:worker_never_started:WORKER_DISPATCH_ERROR:...`

Closes #t183

title: fix: Tabby repo pollution + missing npm on ARM64 Ubuntu
body:
## Summary

Fixes cascading apt failures on ARM64 Linux (OrbStack Ubuntu) caused by a stale Tabby packagecloud repo, and ensures npm is available for OpenCode CLI installation.

## Root Cause

The Tabby packagecloud repo (added in a previous setup.sh run before the ARM64 fix existed) only has x86_64 packages. On ARM64, every `apt-get update` fails with:
```
Err: https://packagecloud.io/eugeny/tabby/ubuntu questing Release
  404  Not Found
```

This cascades to break: NodeSource setup, gh/glab install, fd/ripgrep install, and ultimately OpenCode CLI install (because npm was never installed).

## Changes

### setup.sh (22 insertions, 1 deletion)

1. **Clean up stale Tabby repo in `setup_nodejs()`** (~line 3837-3846): Before running NodeSource/apt install, check for and remove the Tabby packagecloud repo on ARM64. This runs early in the flow (before `setup_recommended_tools`), preventing the cascade.

2. **Clean up stale Tabby repo in `setup_recommended_tools()`** (~line 1946-1953): Also clean up in the Tabby ARM64 section itself, with an `apt-get update` to refresh the package cache.

3. **Install npm alongside nodejs in NodeSource path** (~line 3855): Changed `sudo apt-get install -y nodejs` to `sudo apt-get install -y nodejs npm 2>/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y nodejs`. This handles the case where NodeSource setup fails silently and apt falls back to the distro `nodejs` package (which doesn't bundle npm, unlike NodeSource).

## Testing

- Syntax: `bash -n setup.sh` passes
- ShellCheck: No new violations on modified lines
- Root cause confirmed: OrbStack Ubuntu ARM64 test output shows the exact cascade

## Impact

Without this fix, a fresh ARM64 Ubuntu install via `bash <(curl -fsSL https://aidevops.sh/install)` results in:
- No gh CLI (can't create PRs)
- No fd/ripgrep (degraded file discovery)
- No npm (can't install OpenCode)
- `opencode: command not found`

title: fix: decouple OpenCode commands from config guard, reorder after CLI install, add auth check
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `/onboarding` command not being available on first run of `setup.sh` on fresh Linux systems (OrbStack Ubuntu ARM64 VM).

### Root Cause

On first run, `update_opencode_config()` was guarded by `find_opencode_config()` which requires `opencode.json` to exist. But:
1. `update_opencode_config` ran **before** `setup_opencode_cli` (which installs OpenCode)
2. Even after install, `opencode.json` doesn't exist until first `opencode` run
3. The commands generator (`generate-opencode-commands.sh`) writes to `~/.config/opencode/command/` and does NOT need `opencode.json`

Result: `/onboarding` command file was never created, causing a red error on first use.

### Fixes

- **Decouple commands from config guard**: Move commands generation before the `find_opencode_config` check in `update_opencode_config()`, so `/onboarding` and all 70 slash commands are created even without `opencode.json`
- **Reorder execution**: Move `update_opencode_config` after `setup_opencode_cli` in the interactive path, so `opencode.json` may exist when agent configuration runs
- **Add auth check**: Before offering to launch onboarding, check if `auth.json` exists with valid providers. If not, show `opencode auth login` instruction instead of launching OpenCode which would fail

### Testing

Verified on OrbStack Ubuntu ARM64 VM (`bash setup.sh --non-interactive`):
- Commands generated successfully (70 commands including `/onboarding`)
- Graceful skip message: `OpenCode config (opencode.json) not found — agent configuration skipped (commands still generated)`
- Auth check correctly detects missing auth and would show login instructions
- ShellCheck clean (no new warnings)

## Summary

Fixes `Agent not found: "Onboarding"` error on first-run opencode launch after setup.

### Root cause

`setup.sh` launched opencode with `--agent "Onboarding" --prompt "/onboarding"`. The "Onboarding" agent only exists after `generate-opencode-agents.sh` writes it into `opencode.json`. ## Summary

title: fix: normalize grep BRE patterns and shellcheck flags in verify-run-helper.sh
body:
## Summary

- Converts `\|` (grep BRE syntax) to `|` (rg ERE syntax) in rg check directives at runtime, fixing 172 broken pattern matches in VERIFY.md
- Adds `-x` (follow sourced files) and `-S warning` (skip info-level SC1091/SC2329) to shellcheck check directives
- **Result**: 25/26 verifications now pass (was 15/26 before this fix)
- Remaining v011 failure is a pre-existing test suite issue (10 flaky tests in test-supervisor-state-machine.sh)

## Root Cause

VERIFY.md check directives were written with `grep` BRE syntax (`\|` for alternation) but executed via `rg` which uses ERE (`|` unescaped for alternation). The `\|` in rg matches a literal pipe character, producing zero matches for every pattern.

ShellCheck checks ran without `-x` flag, causing SC1091 (not following sourced files) to trigger as a failure even though the scripts are correct.

title: fix: secretlint-helper.sh install and scan in git worktrees (t191)
body:
## Summary

- Add worktree-aware helpers (`is_git_worktree`, `get_repo_root`, `get_git_dir`) to `secretlint-helper.sh` that resolve the main repo root via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`
- Fix all functions that look up `node_modules/.bin/secretlint` or run `npm list` to also check the main repo's `node_modules` when running in a linked worktree
- Fix `setup_precommit_hook` which failed in worktrees because `.git` is a file (not a directory) — now uses `git rev-parse --git-dir` for the hooks path
- Fix `linters-local.sh` to resolve secretlint from the main repo's `node_modules` in worktree environments

## Problem

In git worktrees, `node_modules` lives in the main repo directory, not the worktree. This caused:
1. `secretlint-helper.sh status` — reported "Secretlint not found" even when installed in main repo
2. `secretlint-helper.sh scan` — failed to find the binary, fell back to `npx` (slow) or failed entirely
3. `secretlint-helper.sh install` — would create a duplicate `node_modules` in the worktree instead of using the main repo's
4. `secretlint-helper.sh hook` — failed with "Not a git repository" because it checked `[[ -d .git ]]` (worktrees have `.git` as a file)
5. `check_rules_installed` — `npm list` found nothing because it only checked CWD
6. `linters-local.sh` — same detection failure for secretlint binary

## Changes

### `secretlint-helper.sh`
- Added `is_git_worktree()`, `get_repo_root()`, `get_git_dir()` helper functions
- Updated `check_secretlint_installed()` — searches global, CWD, and main repo `node_modules`
- Updated `get_secretlint_cmd()` — returns absolute path from main repo when in worktree
- Updated `check_rules_installed()` — uses `npm list --prefix` for main repo

title: fix: extract PR URL from worker final text to prevent false clean_exit_no_signal retries (t192)
body:
## Summary

- **Bug**: Supervisor evaluated successful workers as `clean_exit_no_signal` because `extract_log_metadata()` returned empty `pr_url=` (disabled by t151), and the `gh pr list --head` fallback had a race condition with GitHub's API indexing
- **Fix**: Extract PR URL from the worker's **last `"type":"text"` JSON entry** — the final summary output is authoritative and safe from the t151 false-positive concern (memory recalls, TODO reads)
- **Impact**: Eliminates unnecessary retries for 20+ production tasks (t134, t191, t181, t182, t184, etc.) that had PR URLs in their final output

## Root Cause

Workers dispatched via `opencode --format json` emit their final summary as a `"type":"text"` JSON entry containing the PR URL. However:

1. `extract_log_metadata()` (t151) intentionally set `pr_url=` empty to avoid false positives from PR URLs mentioned in memory recalls, TODO reads, and git log context
2. The `gh pr list --head` fallback in `evaluate_worker()` has a race condition — GitHub's API may not have indexed a just-created PR
3. Result: `meta_pr_url=""`, `meta_signal="none"`, `meta_exit_code="0"` → `retry:clean_exit_no_signal`

## Fix

Extract PR URL from only the **last** `"type":"text"` JSON entry in the log (the worker's final output). This is safe because:
- The last text entry is the worker's own summary, not context from other tasks
- Earlier text entries (which may reference other PRs) are ignored
- The `gh pr list --head` fallback remains as a safety net

## Tests

2 new tests in `test-supervisor-state-machine.sh`:
- `eval-t192a`: Verifies PR URL extraction from final text entry → `complete:<pr_url>`
- `eval-t192b`: Verifies no false extraction from earlier text entries → `retry:clean_exit_no_signal`

## Evidence

State log showing the bug in production:
```
t134|evaluating|retrying|clean_exit_no_signal|2026-02-09T03:11:52Z
t191|evaluating|retrying|clean_exit_no_signal|2026-02-09T03:02:23Z
t181|evaluating|retrying|clean_exit_no_signal|2026-02-08T23:05:33Z
t182|evaluating|retrying|clean_exit_no_signal|2026-02-08T23:11:38Z
t184|evaluating|retrying|clean_exit_no_signal|2026-02-08T23:40:12Z
```

All of these tasks had PR URLs in their final text output that was being ignored.

title: fix: supervisor claim/unclaim now matches indented subtasks in TODO.md
body:
## Summary

- Fix supervisor's inability to dispatch subtasks (e.g., t132.2, t168.2) from TODO.md
- Change grep patterns from `^- \[` to `^[[:space:]]*- \[` in claim/unclaim/lookup functions

## Problem

The supervisor's `claim`, `unclaim`, and task lookup functions used `^- \[ \]` regex which only matched top-level tasks. Subtasks in TODO.md are indented:

This caused all subtask dispatches to fail with "Task tXXX.X not found as open in TODO.md".

## Fix

Changed 7 grep patterns to use `^[[:space:]]*- \[` which matches both:
- `- [ ] t132 ...` (top-level, zero indent)
- `  - [ ] t132.2 ...` (subtask, 2+ space indent)

## Functions Fixed

- `cmd_claim()` — task existence check + line number lookup
- `cmd_unclaim()` — line number lookup
- `check_task_claimed()` — task line lookup
- `get_task_gh_issue()` — task line lookup

title: feat: extend setup.sh to deploy plugins during aidevops update (t136.3)
body:
## Summary

- Add `deploy_plugins()` function to `setup.sh` that deploys enabled plugins from `~/.config/aidevops/plugins.json` after core agent deployment
- Preserve plugin namespace directories during clean mode (alongside custom/ and draft/)
- Exclude plugin namespaces from rsync/tar to prevent core deployment from overwriting them
- Clean up disabled plugin directories automatically
- Update `plugins.md` to document automatic deployment behavior

## Details

Part of the Plugin System plan (t136). Follows t136.2 (plugin CLI commands, PR #759).

### How it works

1. `deploy_aidevops_agents()` reads `plugins.json` to collect plugin namespaces
2. Plugin directories are added to the preserve list (clean mode) and exclude list (rsync/tar)
3. After core deployment, `deploy_plugins()` is called:
   - Removes directories for disabled plugins
   - Installs missing enabled plugins via shallow clone
   - Skips already-deployed plugins (use `aidevops plugin update` to refresh)
   - Reports summary (deployed/skipped/failed counts)

### Edge cases handled

- No `plugins.json` file: silently skips
- No `jq` available: warns and skips
- Empty plugins array: silently skips
- All plugins disabled: reports and skips
- Clone failure (network/auth): warns but continues (non-blocking)
- Plugin already deployed: skips re-clone

- No regressions in core agent deployment flow

- Adds `coderabbit-collector-helper.sh` — a new helper script that polls for CodeRabbit review completion on PRs, extracts review comments and inline suggestions into a SQLite database, and categorises them by severity and type.

## What it does

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `collect --pr N [--wait]` | Collect CodeRabbit reviews/comments from a PR into SQLite |
| `poll --pr N [--timeout S]` | Poll until CodeRabbit posts a review |
| `query [--severity S] [--category C] [--format json]` | Query stored comments with filters |
| `summary [--pr N]` | Severity/category breakdown, most-affected files |
| `export [--format json\|csv]` | Export all data |
| `status` | Show collector status and DB info |

## Design decisions

- **jq filter files for SQL generation**: Avoids shell expansion of `$variables` and backticks in CodeRabbit comment bodies (which contain code snippets). The jq filter handles SQL single-quote escaping (`gsub("'"; "''")`) safely.
- **SQLite WAL mode + busy_timeout**: Follows `mail-helper.sh` and `memory-helper.sh` patterns for concurrent access safety.
- **Unit separator (0x1f)** for display queries: Handles pipes (`|`) in markdown content that would break `IFS='|'` parsing.
- **Negative IDs for issue comments**: Avoids collision between PR review comment IDs and issue comment IDs in the same table.
- **Severity/category classification in jq**: Done inside the jq filter (not shell) to avoid shell expansion issues with comment bodies.
- **Idempotent collection**: `INSERT OR IGNORE` on unique `gh_comment_id` / `gh_review_id` prevents duplicates on re-collection.

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations
- `bash -n`: clean syntax
- Tested against real PRs (#762, #763) — collected reviews, inline comments, and walkthrough summaries
- Verified idempotent re-collection (0 new on second run)
- Verified query, summary, JSON export, and CSV export

## Task

Implements t166.2: "Monitor and collect CodeRabbit review feedback into structured format"

title: fix: resolve cron pulse claim failure due to missing project root
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `cmd_claim()` and `cmd_unclaim()` called `find_project_root()` which walks up from `$PWD` looking for `TODO.md`. When cron runs the supervisor pulse, `$PWD` is `$HOME` where no `TODO.md` exists, so every dispatch attempt fails.
- **Impact**: All 14 queued tasks in batch backlog-09 were stuck — cron tried to dispatch each one, failed to claim, and moved to the next. Zero tasks dispatched autonomously since the batch started.
- **Fix**: Both functions now accept an optional `project_root` argument. When not provided and `find_project_root()` fails, they fall back to the task's `repo` column from the supervisor DB. The dispatch function passes `trepo` to `cmd_claim`.

## Evidence

Cron log showed repeated failures:
```
[SUPERVISOR] TODO.md not found at ./TODO.md
[SUPERVISOR] Failed to claim t102.2 — aborting dispatch
[SUPERVISOR] Failed to claim t132.3 — aborting dispatch
... (all 14 queued tasks)
```

## Testing

- `bash -n` syntax check: pass
- ShellCheck: no new violations
- Manual pulse from repo directory still works (find_project_root succeeds)
- Cron environment: will now fall back to DB repo path

title: fix: resolve gh auth, sysctl, and identity failures in cron supervisor pulse
body:
## Summary

Three bugs prevented the autonomous supervisor pipeline from working via cron:

1. **GH_TOKEN resolution** - macOS keyring is inaccessible from cron, so gh auth always failed. Added multi-source token resolution with file caching: interactive sessions cache the token (600 perms), cron reads from cache. Fallback chain: env var > gh auth token > cached file > gopass > credentials.sh.

2. **PATH missing /usr/sbin** - sysctl lives at /usr/sbin/sysctl which was not in cron PATH. get_cpu_cores() fell back to echo 4 (actual: 10) and vm.loadavg returned empty. Added /usr/sbin to PATH augmentation.

3. **get_aidevops_identity returning 401 JSON** - When gh api user failed, it returned JSON which was stored as assignee value, breaking sed with unescaped newlines. Added regex validation and safety check in cmd_claim().

## Testing

- bash -n passes, ShellCheck no new violations
- Functional test with cron-like env (env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin): GH_TOKEN resolved (40 chars from cache), 10 cores detected (not fallback 4), real load reported (80.74 not 0.00), t132.4 dispatched successfully
- Before: Load: 0.00 / 0.00 (4 cores), GitHub auth unavailable, assignee stored as JSON
- After: Load: 80.74 / 115.61 (10 cores), dispatch successful, correct assignee

body:
## Summary

- Adds `cross-review` command to compare-models-helper.sh for second-opinion review patterns
- Dispatches the same prompt to multiple AI models in parallel via runner-helper.sh
- Collects results, generates word count comparison and unified diff

## Usage

```bash
# Review code with Sonnet and Opus (default)
compare-models-helper.sh cross-review \
  --prompt "Review this code for security issues: $(cat src/auth.ts)"

# Custom model set with timeout
compare-models-helper.sh cross-review \
  --prompt "Audit the architecture" \
  --models "sonnet,opus,pro" \
  --timeout 900

# Specify output directory
compare-models-helper.sh cross-review \
  --prompt "Review PR changes" \
  --models "opus,pro" \
  --output /tmp/my-review
```

## How It Works

1. Creates temporary runners for each model (via runner-helper.sh)
2. Dispatches the same prompt to all models in parallel (background processes)
3. Waits for all to complete (with per-model timeout)
4. Extracts text responses from JSON output
5. Displays each model's response
6. Generates diff summary: word counts + unified diff (for 2-model comparisons)
7. Cleans up temporary runners

## Use Cases

- **Code review**: Get a second opinion from a different model
- **Security audit**: Cross-validate findings across providers

title: feat: add Worker Efficiency Protocol to headless worker dispatch
body:
## Summary

- Injects a **Worker Efficiency Protocol** into the supervisor dispatch prompt (`build_dispatch_cmd`) so all headless workers receive structured efficiency guidance
- Documents the protocol in `headless-dispatch.md` with rationale and ROI analysis

## What Changed

### `supervisor-helper.sh` — Dispatch Prompt Enhancement

Added a new `## Worker Efficiency Protocol` section to the prompt injected into every worker session. Workers are now instructed to:

1. **Decompose with TodoWrite (MANDATORY)** — Break task into 3-7 subtasks at session start. Provides progress breadcrumb trail that survives context compaction.
2. **Checkpoint after each subtask** — Call `session-checkpoint-helper.sh save` so progress persists to disk. Enables resume-from-checkpoint instead of restart-from-scratch.
3. **Parallel sub-work** — Use Task tool for independent subtasks (e.g., tests + docs simultaneously). Only when subtasks don't modify the same files.
4. **Fail fast** — Verify assumptions before writing code (read target files, check deps exist, confirm task isn't already done).
5. **Minimise token waste** — Read file ranges not whole files, concise commits, exit with BLOCKED after one failed retry.

### `headless-dispatch.md` — Documentation

New "Worker Efficiency Protocol" section documenting:
- The five key practices
- Before/after comparison table
- Token cost analysis (~200 tokens overhead vs 10K-50K saved per avoided restart = 30-150x ROI)

## Why

Workers currently operate linearly with no internal structure. When context compacts mid-task, they lose all progress and restart from scratch — burning 2x the tokens. Complex tasks with multiple phases (research, implement, test, PR) have no explicit tracking, so workers sometimes skip steps or repeat them.

The protocol adds ~200-300 tokens per session but prevents full restarts that cost 10,000-50,000 tokens each.

## Testing

- ShellCheck: no new violations (resolved SC2153 false positive by using `<your-task-id>` placeholder)
- `bash -n`: syntax OK
- `markdownlint`: clean
- Prompt renders correctly within the existing `build_dispatch_cmd` function

title: perf: supervisor auth caching and auto model tier routing
body:
## Summary

- Cache `check_gh_auth()` results for 5 minutes to eliminate redundant GitHub API calls (~288/day saved)
- Auto-classify task complexity to route simple tasks to sonnet (~5x cheaper than opus)
- Wire classifier into `resolve_task_model` as step 3 in the resolution chain

## Changes

### 1. Cached `check_gh_auth()` (lines 239-278)

**Before**: Every call to `check_gh_auth()` hit `gh api user` or `gh auth status`. Called 1-5 times per pulse, pulses every 2-5 minutes = ~288-720 API calls/day.

**After**: Result cached to `$SUPERVISOR_DIR/.gh-auth-cache` with 5-minute TTL. Subsequent calls within the window return instantly from cache. Cache invalidates on failure so token refreshes are picked up.

### 2. `classify_task_complexity()` (new function)

Pattern-matches task descriptions against known simple/complex indicators:

| Classification | Patterns | Model |
|---------------|----------|-------|
| **Simple** | update docs, fix typo, rename, wire up command, add reference, update index | sonnet |
| **Complex** | architecture, security audit, migration, novel, from scratch, multi-provider | opus |
| **Default** | anything not matched | opus (safe default) |

Tested against real task descriptions from backlog-09:
- "Update AGENTS.md progressive disclosure table" → sonnet
- "Wire up /compare-models slash command" → sonnet
- "Add fallback chain configuration with per-agent overrides" → opus
- "Success pattern tracking with model routing integration" → opus

### 3. Wired into `resolve_task_model()` (step 3)

Resolution priority is now:
1. Task's explicit model (if set and non-default)
2. Subagent frontmatter `model:` field
3. **NEW: Auto-classification from task description**
4. Default coding tier (opus)

## Cost Impact

Based on backlog-09 (20 tasks):
- ~5 tasks would have been routed to sonnet (docs updates, slash commands, index updates)
- Sonnet is ~5x cheaper per token than opus
- Estimated 20-25% cost reduction per batch for mixed-complexity workloads

## Testing

- `bash -n`: syntax OK
- ShellCheck: no new violations
- Classification function tested against 14 real task descriptions — all classified correctly
- Safe default: unknown tasks stay on opus (no risk of under-provisioning)

title: fix: redirect supervisor log functions to stderr (unblocks all workers)

## Summary

- `log_error` already used stderr correctly; now all log functions follow Unix convention (logs to stderr, data to stdout)

## Problem

All worker dispatches in batch `backlog-10` (14 tasks) were failing immediately with `ProviderModelNotFoundError`. The model string passed to OpenCode contained ANSI-colored log lines because `resolve_task_model()` uses `log_info` (stdout) and returns its value via `echo` (also stdout). [SUPERVISOR] Model for t135.3: openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (default coding tier)
```
openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4-6
```

...instead of just `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`.

- **Unblocks**: All 14 tasks in backlog-10 batch (t135.3-t135.14, t020.1-t020.6)
- **Fixes latent bug**: `resolve_model()` also has `log_verbose` calls that would pollute stdout when `SUPERVISOR_VERBOSE=true`

title: feat: add pre-dispatch verification to prevent dispatching already-done tasks
body:
## Summary

- Add `check_task_already_done()` function to supervisor that runs before every worker dispatch
- Checks 3 sources: TODO.md `[x]` marker, git commit history (conventional commit + PR refs), GitHub merged PRs
- Auto-cancels tasks that are already done instead of wasting Opus sessions
- Prevents the backlog-10 bug where 6 t135 subtasks were dispatched despite being completed months earlier

## Root Cause

The supervisor had no pre-dispatch verification. Tasks added to a batch were dispatched blindly even if they'd been completed in a prior batch. Workers would discover "already done" and exit, but the evaluator classified this as `clean_exit_no_signal` and retried — wasting 3 full Opus sessions per task.

## Implementation

`check_task_already_done(task_id, repo)` returns 0 (already done) or 1 (not done):
1. **TODO.md check**: grep for `- [x] tNNN` pattern
2. **Git history check**: search last 500 commits for task ID with completion evidence (feat/fix/refactor commits or PR merge references)
3. **GitHub PR check**: search merged PRs by task ID in title (only if `gh` CLI available)

Inserted in `cmd_dispatch()` after status validation, before task claiming.

title: fix: scope pre-dispatch TODO.md check to first occurrence + skip OpenCode health probe
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for supervisor dispatch blockers:

### 1. Pre-dispatch TODO.md false positives (CRITICAL)

`check_task_already_done()` was matching `[x]` entries in the **archived plan section** of TODO.md, causing false cancellation of tasks that were still `[ ]` in the active task list.

**Root cause**: TODO.md contains the same task ID in two places:
- **Active task list** (line ~79): `- [ ] t020.4 Pull command...` (NOT done)
- **Completed plan archive** (line ~475): `- [x] t020.4 Add pull command...` (historical)

The `grep -q` matched the archive entry first and returned "done".

**Fix**: Use `head -1` to check only the first occurrence. If the first match is `[ ]` or `[-]`, return "not done" immediately — ignoring any later `[x]` entries in archive sections.

**Impact**: t020.4, t020.5, t020.6 were falsely cancelled. This is the third iteration of false-positive prevention (after PR #807 fixed substring matching).

### 2. Health check timeout blocking OpenCode dispatch

The model health check was timing out for OpenCode-managed providers because:
1. Fast path (`model-availability-helper.sh`) fails with "no API key" — OpenCode manages keys internally
2. Slow path (`opencode run` probe) times out at 15s

**Fix**: When `ai_cli` is `opencode` and the availability helper fails (exit != 0/2/3), skip the slow CLI probe and assume healthy. OpenCode manages its own auth — if the model is unavailable, dispatch will fail and retry logic handles it.

**Impact**: t194 was stuck in queue because every pulse cycle hit the 15s timeout.

## Testing

Verified grep pattern against actual TODO.md:
- `t020.4`: first match is `[ ]` → correctly returns "not done"
- `t020.5`: first match is `[ ]` → correctly returns "not done"  
- `t020.6`: first match is `[ ]` → correctly returns "not done"
- `t135.9`: first match is `[x]` → correctly returns "done"
- `t194`: first match is `[ ]` → correctly returns "not done"

ShellCheck: zero new violations.

title: fix: prevent RETURN trap clobbering with cleanup stack (t196)
body:
## Summary

- Add `push_cleanup`/`_run_cleanups`/`_save_cleanup_scope` utilities to `shared-constants.sh` that accumulate cleanup commands in a stack, preventing the silent clobbering that occurs when a bash function sets `trap ... RETURN` more than once
- Migrate all 49 `trap ... RETURN` instances across 28 scripts to use the new pattern
- Add `shared-constants.sh` source to `loop-common.sh` (only script missing it)

## Problem

In bash, setting `trap 'cmd' RETURN` twice in the same function silently replaces the first trap. If a function creates two temp files with separate traps, the first file leaks:

```bash
# BUG: only $b gets cleaned up, $a leaks
my_func() {
    local a; a=$(mktemp); trap "rm -f '$a'" RETURN
    local b; b=$(mktemp); trap "rm -f '$b'" RETURN  # clobbers first trap!
}
```

## Solution

A cleanup stack pattern where functions accumulate cleanup commands:

```bash
my_func() {
    _save_cleanup_scope; trap '_run_cleanups' RETURN
    local a; a=$(mktemp); push_cleanup "rm -f '${a}'"
    local b; b=$(mktemp); push_cleanup "rm -f '${b}'"
    # Both files cleaned up on return (LIFO order)
}
```

Key properties:
- **LIFO execution** — last pushed = first cleaned (matches resource acquisition order)
- **Nesting-safe** — `_save_cleanup_scope` preserves parent function's cleanup list
- **Backward compatible** — single-trap functions work identically to before
- **Zero new shellcheck warnings**

## Testing

All 13 unit tests pass:
1. Single cleanup removes file
2. Multiple cleanups all execute
3. Nested functions don't clobber each other
4. LIFO cleanup order verified
5. Directory cleanup with rm -rf
6. Empty cleanup stack is safe
7. Cleanup after early return

Regression test confirms old pattern leaks file `a` while new pattern cleans both.

## Files Changed

- `shared-constants.sh` — new cleanup stack utilities (+103 lines)
- 28 scripts — migrated from raw `trap ... RETURN` to `push_cleanup` pattern

title: fix: resolve clean_exit_no_signal false retry loop (t198)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `clean_exit_no_signal` false retry loop that wasted retry attempts on tasks that either hit backend errors during retries or were already done/obsolete.

## Root Causes Found

### 1. Backend error detection threshold too strict
- `evaluate_worker()` used `log_lines < 10` to detect short backend-error-only logs
- Retry logs include an 8-line REPROMPT METADATA header, inflating line count to 12+
- Backend errors like "All Antigravity endpoints failed" were misclassified as `clean_exit_no_signal`
- **Fix**: Added `content_lines` metadata field that excludes REPROMPT METADATA headers

### 2. No detection path for "task already done"
- Workers that determine a task is obsolete exit cleanly (EXIT:0) with no signal and no PR
- The supervisor had no way to distinguish this from "worker ran out of context"
- Tasks like t135.4 ("TASK ALREADY DONE") and t135.5 ("already done") were retried repeatedly
- **Fix**: Added `task_obsolete` detection in `extract_log_metadata` that checks the workers final text output for explicit "already done" / "no changes needed" language, classified as `complete:task_obsolete`

## Evidence

From production supervisor logs:
- t135.3: 3 retries, all "All Antigravity endpoints failed" with EXIT:0 (12 lines each)
- t135.4: Worker said "TASK ALREADY DONE" on first run, then 2 retries hit backend errors
- t135.5: Worker said "Task t135.5 is already done" on first run, then retried

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/supervisor-helper.sh`: Added `content_lines` and `task_obsolete` metadata fields in `extract_log_metadata()`, updated `evaluate_worker()` to use `content_lines` for backend error threshold and detect task obsolescence before falling through to `clean_exit_no_signal`
- `tests/test-supervisor-state-machine.sh`: 4 new tests for t198 scenarios
- `tests/test-dispatch-worktree-evaluate.sh`: 1 new integration test for backend error with REPROMPT METADATA

## Test Results

All 4 core tests pass:
- Backend error + REPROMPT METADATA -> `retry:backend_quota_error` (was `clean_exit_no_signal`)
- Worker says "already done" -> `complete:task_obsolete` (was `retry:clean_exit_no_signal`)
- Worker says "no changes needed" -> `complete:task_obsolete` (was `retry:clean_exit_no_signal`)
- Normal incomplete exit -> `retry:clean_exit_no_signal` (unchanged, regression safe)

title: fix: use actual CPU idle% for adaptive throttling on macOS
body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: Adaptive throttler used `load_average / cpu_cores` as its signal, which on macOS includes I/O-blocked processes (Backblaze, Spotlight, etc.). Load average of 155 on 10 cores = 1550% ratio, causing max throttle to 1-2 workers — even when actual CPU was only 65% used with 35% idle.
- **Fix**: On macOS, use `top -l 1` to get real CPU idle percentage (0-100%). Recalibrate throttle bands: <40% = scale up, 40-70% = base, 70-85% = halve, >85% = minimum.
- **Impact**: Workers will now dispatch at full base concurrency when CPU headroom exists, instead of being artificially throttled by misleading load averages. Linux behavior unchanged.

## Testing

Verified `top -l 1 | awk '/CPU usage/ ...'` returns accurate idle% (37% idle = 63% used) while load average simultaneously showed 155/10 cores. ShellCheck clean on changed lines.

title: perf: enable Anthropic prompt caching in setup
body:
## Summary

- Enables Anthropic prompt caching (`setCacheKey: true`) in the OpenCode config generator
- Caches the system prompt prefix (AGENTS.md + build.txt + tool definitions, ~8-10K tokens) across API requests
- Reduces input token costs by ~90% on cache hits (0.1x vs 1x base input price)

## How it works

- OpenCode's AI SDK sets `cache_control` breakpoints on the system prompt when `setCacheKey: true`
- Anthropic caches the prefix with a 5-minute TTL (auto-refreshed on use)
- Cache auto-invalidates when file content changes (content-based hashing)
- Works on all Anthropic models (min 1024-4096 tokens depending on model)
- No manual invalidation needed -- `aidevops update` / `setup.sh` naturally refreshes on next session

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh`: Added PROVIDER OPTIONS section that sets `setCacheKey: true` for Anthropic
- Also applied to live config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) for immediate effect

## Cost impact

Over a 50-message session, ~85% savings on input tokens for the instruction prefix (~8-10K tokens cached).

title: fix: sync homebrew formula version and enable subtask GitHub Issues
body:
## Summary

- Fix homebrew formula version drift that was failing CI on **all open PRs** (v2.107.0 → v2.108.0)
- Enable GitHub Issue creation for subtasks (t199.1-t199.11 etc.) in issue-sync-helper.sh
- Prevent future homebrew drift by adding `homebrew/aidevops.rb` to version-manager.sh commit step

## Root Causes

### 1. Homebrew Version Drift (blocking all PRs)
`version-manager.sh` `commit_version_changes()` staged all version files **except** `homebrew/aidevops.rb`. The `update_version_in_files()` function correctly updated the formula, but the commit step never staged it. Every release left the formula one version behind on `origin/main`, causing the Version Consistency Check to fail on every PR.

### 2. Subtasks Not Getting GitHub Issues
`issue-sync-helper.sh` `cmd_push()` explicitly skipped indented subtask lines (`^- \[` only matches unindented). All 11 subtasks of t199 (t199.1-t199.11) had no GitHub Issues. The same `^-` pattern was used across `cmd_push`, `cmd_pull`, `cmd_close`, `cmd_enrich`, `cmd_status`, `cmd_reconcile`, `add_gh_ref_to_todo`, and `fix_gh_ref_in_todo`.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `version-manager.sh` | Add `homebrew/aidevops.rb` to `git add` in `commit_version_changes()` |
| `homebrew/aidevops.rb` | Update URL from v2.107.0 to v2.108.0 |
| `issue-sync-helper.sh` | Change all `^-` grep/sed patterns to `^\s*-` across 8 functions |

## Verification

- ShellCheck: zero new violations
- Syntax check: both scripts pass `bash -n`
- The homebrew fix will make Version Consistency Check pass, unblocking PRs #835, #834, #842, #840, #845

title: fix: detect billing/credits errors and block immediately instead of retrying
body:
## Summary

- Adds `CreditsError|Insufficient balance|statusCode.*401` to supervisor backend error detection patterns
- Billing errors now return `blocked:billing_credits_exhausted` instead of `retry:backend_quota_error`
- Health probe also detects billing errors to prevent dispatch to exhausted providers

## Root Cause

OpenCode CLI sometimes routes `anthropic/*` models through its Zen proxy (`opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages`) instead of direct Anthropic OAuth when the OAuth path is temporarily unavailable. When Zen credits are exhausted, this produces `CreditsError` with `EXIT:0`.

Previously, the supervisor treated these as generic `backend_quota_error` and deferred retries, eventually exhausting `max_retries` across 4 tasks (t199.7, t199.8, t199.9, t199.11). Now billing errors are detected and tasks are blocked immediately since retrying won't resolve a billing issue.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `supervisor-helper.sh:4545` | Added `CreditsError\|Insufficient balance\|statusCode.*401` to backend error grep pattern |
| `supervisor-helper.sh:3543` | Added `CreditsError\|Insufficient balance` to health probe failure detection |
| `supervisor-helper.sh:4843-4850` | New billing-specific check: if CreditsError found in log, return `blocked:billing_credits_exhausted` before generic `retry:backend_quota_error` |

title: fix: enforce anthropic-only model resolution, reject opencode/* proxy models
body:
## Summary

- Rejects `opencode/*` models from availability helper resolution in `resolve_model()`
- Only accepts `anthropic/*` results, falling through to static defaults otherwise
- This is the **actual root cause** of tasks hitting OpenCode Zen proxy billing

## Root Cause (Full Chain)

1. `model-availability-helper.sh` sees `anthropic` as `no-key` (no standalone `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — we use Anthropic OAuth through OpenCode)
2. It sees `opencode` as `healthy` (OpenCode CLI is installed)
3. `resolve_model()` calls the availability helper which returns `opencode/claude-sonnet-4` instead of `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`
4. `opencode/` prefixed models route through OpenCode's Zen proxy (`opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages`)
5. Zen proxy uses OpenCode credits, not Anthropic OAuth
6. OpenCode credits exhausted -> `CreditsError`

## Fix

`resolve_model()` now checks `[[ "$resolved" == anthropic/* ]]` before accepting availability helper results. Non-anthropic results are logged and skipped, falling through to the static defaults which correctly map all tiers to `anthropic/*` models.

## Includes from PR #876

- `CreditsError|Insufficient balance|statusCode.*401` added to backend error detection
- Billing errors return `blocked:billing_credits_exhausted` (immediate block, no retry)
- Health probe also detects billing errors

## Verification

```
sonnet -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5
coding -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6
opus   -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6
health -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5
```

title: feat: add orphaned PR scanner to supervisor pulse (t210)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `scan_orphaned_prs()` function to detect PRs that workers created but the supervisor missed during evaluation
- Integrated as **Phase 6** of the supervisor pulse cycle (between process hygiene and TODO reconciliation)
- Also exposed as manual CLI command: `supervisor-helper.sh scan-orphaned-prs [batch_id]`

## Problem

Workers sometimes create PRs but the supervisor fails to link them during `evaluate_worker()`. This happens when:
- Worker exits without emitting `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` or `TASK_COMPLETE` signals
- Worker uses a branch name not stored in the DB `branch` column
- The `gh pr list --head` fallback in `evaluate_worker()` fails (API timeout, rate limit)
- Tasks end up stuck in `failed`/`blocked`/`retrying` with a valid PR sitting on GitHub

## Solution

The orphaned PR scanner runs during each pulse (throttled to 10-minute intervals) and:
1. Finds tasks with no PR URL that are in actionable states (`failed`, `blocked`, `retrying`, `complete`, `running`, `evaluating`)
2. Groups tasks by repo and does a single bulk `gh pr list` call per repo (open + merged PRs)
3. Matches PRs to tasks by task ID in title or branch name using jq regex
4. Validates matches via existing `validate_pr_belongs_to_task()` (prevents false attribution)
5. Links found PRs and transitions `failed`/`blocked`/`retrying` tasks to `complete`
6. Runs post-completion hooks (`update_todo_on_complete`, notifications, success patterns)

## Testing

- `bash -n` syntax check: PASS
- ShellCheck (severity=warning): zero new violations (only pre-existing SC2034 in other functions)
- Existing test suite: 96/109 pass, 11 fail, 2 skip — all failures pre-existing (identical before/after)
- No regressions introduced

## Design Decisions

- **Bulk API calls**: One `gh pr list` per repo instead of per task — minimises GitHub API usage
- **Throttled**: 10-minute interval via timestamp file (matches pattern used by Phase 8 issue-sync)
- **Reuses existing validation**: `validate_pr_belongs_to_task()` ensures word-boundary matching of task IDs
- **Checks merged PRs too**: Workers may create PRs that get auto-merged or manually merged before the scanner runs
- **Bash 3.2 compatible**: No associative arrays; uses pipe-delimited string for repo deduplication

title: feat: add cross-shell compatibility to preserve bash config when switching to zsh
body:
## Summary

- Adds `setup_shell_compatibility()` step to setup.sh that runs after Oh My Zsh installation
- When users switch from bash to zsh, their PATH entries, aliases, exports, and tool integrations (nvm, pyenv, brew, etc.) are preserved via a shared `~/.shell_common` profile
- Both `.zshrc` and bash configs source this shared file, so users maintain one config for both shells

## Problem

Setup offers to install Oh My Zsh and change the default shell to zsh. Users who accept lose all their bash customizations — PATH entries, aliases, exports, and tool integrations like nvm/pyenv/brew shellenv. This is especially painful on macOS where many users have years of bash config from before Catalina switched the default to zsh.

## Solution

Best-practice shared profile pattern:

1. Scans `.bash_profile`, `.bashrc`, and `.profile` for portable customizations
2. Extracts exports, aliases, PATH entries, eval/source commands into `~/.shell_common`
3. Skips bash-specific syntax (shopt, PS1, completion, bind, HISTCONTROL, etc.)
4. Deduplicates lines across files (handles Linux's `.bash_profile` sourcing `.bashrc`)
5. Adds POSIX dot-source (`.`) to both `.zshrc` and bash configs
6. Users edit `~/.shell_common` for shared settings, shell-specific files for the rest

## Platform Support

- **macOS**: Scans `.bash_profile` + `.bashrc` (both common), creates/updates `.zshrc`
- **Linux**: Scans `.bashrc` + `.profile` + `.bash_profile`, handles all common layouts
- Uses POSIX `.` (dot-source) instead of `source` for maximum compatibility
- Gracefully skips if zsh or bash is not installed

## Quality

- Zero new ShellCheck violations
- Bash syntax check passes
- Opt-in `[Y/n]` prompt (default yes), idempotent (skips if `~/.shell_common` exists)
- Follows existing setup.sh patterns (`local var="$1"`, explicit returns, `confirm_step`)

title: fix: setup.sh cross-shell grep -c arithmetic error
body:
## Summary

- Fixes arithmetic error in `setup_shell_compatibility()` at line ~1553 of setup.sh
- `grep -cE` outputs `0` on no match (exit code 1), then `|| echo "0"` appends a second `0` line, producing `"0\n0"` which breaks `$(( ))` arithmetic
- Fix: use `|| true` to suppress exit code without appending output, and `${n:-0}` as safety fallback

## Root Cause

```bash
# Before (broken): n becomes "0\n0" (two lines)
n=$(grep -cE '^\s*alias\s+' "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")

# After (fixed): n becomes "0" (single line)
n=$(grep -cE '^\s*alias\s+' "$file" 2>/dev/null) || true
total=$((total + ${n:-0}))
```

## Impact

This bug was introduced by PR #900 and blocks all autonomous deploys via `run_deploy_for_task()` in the supervisor. The error is non-fatal (setup.sh continues) but produces confusing output and may cause incorrect cross-shell compatibility detection.

## Testing

- Verified fix produces clean single-line values for all bash config files
- Full `setup.sh --non-interactive` completes with zero errors
- ShellCheck clean (no new violations)

## Summary

- Adds `proof_logs` SQLite table with structured audit trail for every supervisor decision point
- Instruments 10+ decision points across the pulse lifecycle (evaluate, complete, retry, blocked, verify, deploy, quality gate, deliverable verification, lifecycle transitions)

## What it does

The existing `state_log` table records state transitions but not **why** decisions were made. The new `proof_logs` table captures:

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `event` | What happened (evaluate, complete, retry, blocked, verify_pass, etc.) |
| `decision` | The decision made (e.g., `complete:PR_URL`, `retry:rate_limited`) |
| `evidence` | Evidence used (e.g., `exit_code=0, signal=FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE`) |
| `decision_maker` | Who/what decided (e.g., `evaluate_worker`, `quality_gate`, `pulse:phase1`) |
| `duration_secs` | Stage duration for pipeline latency analysis (t219 prep) |

## Query interface

```bash
supervisor-helper.sh proof-log t001              # Table view
supervisor-helper.sh proof-log t001 --json       # JSON export
supervisor-helper.sh proof-log t001 --timeline   # Stage timing timeline
supervisor-helper.sh proof-log --recent 20       # Recent entries
supervisor-helper.sh proof-log --stats           # Aggregate statistics
```

## Design decisions

- **Best-effort writes**: proof-log failures never block the pipeline
- **Immutable append-only**: no UPDATE/DELETE on proof_logs (audit integrity)

title: feat(supervisor): faster PR merge pipeline with parallel CI + review triage (t219)
body:
## Summary

Optimizes the PR lifecycle in the supervisor to reduce time from PR creation to deployment by implementing:

1. **Fast-path for clean PRs**: When CI is green and zero review threads exist, skip the `review_triage` state entirely and go directly from `pr_review` → `merging`
2. **Multi-stage transitions**: Already supported - tasks can progress through multiple states (`pr_review` → `merging` → `merged` → `deploying` → `deployed`) in a single pulse
3. **Timing metrics**: Track time spent in each stage and log to `proof-log.jsonl` for pipeline latency analysis

## Impact

- **Clean PRs** (CI green + no review comments) now go from `complete` → `deployed` in **1-2 pulses** instead of 3+
- **Timing data** enables data-driven optimization of bottlenecks
- **Fast-path marked** in `triage_result` with `fast_path:true` flag for analytics

## Implementation Details

### Fast-Path Logic

When a PR reaches `pr_review` state with `ready_to_merge` status:
1. Check if `skip_review_triage` is enabled (bypass)
2. If not, query GitHub GraphQL API for unresolved review threads
3. If thread count is 0, transition directly to `merging` (skip `review_triage`)
4. If threads exist, go through normal triage flow

### Timing Metrics

Each stage tracks:
- `pr_review`: Time from entering pr_review to exiting (includes CI wait)
- `review_triage`: Time spent triaging review feedback
- `merging`: Time to merge PR
- `deploying`: Time to run postflight + deploy + cleanup
- `total`: Total lifecycle time

Logged to `proof-log.jsonl` as:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-10T05:30:00Z",
  "task_id": "t219",
  "event": "pr_lifecycle_timing",
  "stages": {
    "pr_review": "5s",
    "merging": "3s",
    "deploying": "12s",
    "total": "20s"
  }
}
```

## Testing

- Syntax validated with `bash -n`
- Logic verified against existing `cmd_pr_lifecycle` flow
- Fast-path only activates when CI is green (existing `check_pr_status` validation)
- Timing metrics are best-effort (failures don't block lifecycle)

title: fix(supervisor): detect gh auth failures to prevent clean_exit_no_signal retry waste (t198)
body:
## Summary

- Root cause analysis of 560 worker logs identified that **79% of `clean_exit_no_signal` cases** are workers that completed work but couldn't push/create PR due to expired GitHub auth
- These burned 3 retries each at Opus cost (~$15-30 per task) with identical failures
- Added `blocked:gh_auth_expired` detection so auth failures block immediately instead of wasting retries

## Root Cause Analysis

| Category | Count | % | Status |
|----------|-------|---|--------|
| Backend errors (short logs) | 169 | 30% | Already handled |
| PR created, no signal | 127 | 23% | Already handled (t192) |
| Success with signal | 92 | 16% | Working correctly |
| No EXIT line (killed) | 65 | 12% | Edge case |
| **clean_exit_no_signal candidates** | **48** | **9%** | **This PR** |
| Short logs (other) | 24 | 4% | Edge case |
| Non-zero exit | 22 | 4% | Already handled |

Of the 48 `clean_exit_no_signal` candidates:
- **38 (79%)**: GitHub auth expired — worker completed work, couldn't push → **NOW BLOCKED**
- 7: Context exhaustion / short logs — legitimate retries
- 2: Task already done — handled by `task_obsolete` detection
- 1: Shell unavailable

## Changes

1. **`extract_log_metadata()`**: Added `gh_auth_failure` detection scanning full log for specific `gh auth` patterns
2. **`evaluate_worker()`**: Added `blocked:gh_auth_expired` check before `clean_exit_no_signal` fallback
3. **Tests**: 4 new test cases in both test suites (all passing, zero regressions)

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero new violations
- `test-supervisor-state-machine.sh`: 4 new tests pass, 13 pre-existing failures unchanged

title: t221: Disable osgrep in worker MCP configs to save CPU
body:
## Summary

- Adds `generate_worker_mcp_config()` function that copies the user's opencode.json and disables heavy indexing MCPs (osgrep, augment-context-engine) for workers
- Sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in worker dispatch scripts to redirect OpenCode to the modified config
- Covers all 3 dispatch points: `cmd_dispatch()`, `cmd_reprompt()`, `dispatch_review_fix_worker()`
- Graceful fallback: if jq is unavailable or config generation fails, workers proceed with original config

## Impact

Saves ~4 CPU cores per worker (osgrep spawns 4 Node.js child processes for semantic indexing). With 3 concurrent workers, this frees 12 cores on a 10-core machine — eliminating the primary source of CPU oversubscription during batch dispatch.

Workers don't need semantic search — `rg` + `git ls-files` covers 95%+ of their search needs. The TODO.md notes and memory context injected at dispatch already tell them where to look.

## Testing

- ShellCheck clean (no new warnings)
- jq validation ensures generated config is valid JSON
- Per-worker config isolation prevents cross-contamination between concurrent workers

Closes t221

title: t228: Worker incremental commit protocol — prevent context-exhaustion data loss
body:
## Summary

- Workers now commit after each implementation subtask and create a draft PR after the first push
- Supervisor auto-promotes draft PRs to ready-for-review when the worker process dies
- Workers offload heavy codebase research to Task sub-agents to preserve context for implementation

## Root Cause

t221 worker made 67 tool calls (22 reads, 41 bash, 3 edits) consuming 3.4MB of log/context. It implemented the entire feature correctly but ran out of context before committing. The work sat uncommitted in the worktree — the supervisor evaluated it as `complete` with `no_pr`, and the implementation had to be manually committed by the monitoring session.

This is a systemic pattern: workers treat the full-loop as research → implement → (finally) commit → push → PR. If context runs out before the final step, all work is lost.

## Changes

### Worker prompt (supervisor-helper.sh)
- **Commit early**: `git add -A && git commit` after each implementation subtask
- **Draft PR early**: `git push -u origin HEAD && gh pr create --draft` after first commit
- **Mark ready**: `gh pr ready` as final step (supervisor handles it if worker dies)
- **Research offloading**: Spawn Task sub-agents for reading large files (500+ lines) instead of consuming parent context
- **TodoWrite**: Last subtask must always be "Push and create PR"

### Supervisor draft auto-promote (supervisor-helper.sh)
- In `process_post_pr_lifecycle()` draft case: check if worker PID is alive
- If alive: wait (worker is still pushing commits)
- If dead: auto-promote via `gh pr ready` (work is as complete as it's going to get)

### Docs (headless-dispatch.md)
- Updated key practices list with new protocol
- Added comparison table rows for context exhaustion scenarios

## Testing

- ShellCheck clean (no new warnings)
- Draft PR detection uses existing `isDraft` check in `cmd_pr_check()`
- Auto-promote only fires when worker PID is confirmed dead
- Safe for concurrent workers: each worker's PID file is task-specific

Closes t228

title: feat(supervisor): Auto-merge when SonarCloud GH Action passes but external quality gate fails
body:
## Summary

Implements t227 - Auto-merge PRs when SonarCloud GH Action passes but external quality gate fails.

## Problem

The supervisor was blocking PRs where:
- ✅ SonarCloud Analysis (GH Action) - SUCCESS
- ❌ SonarCloud Code Analysis (external quality gate) - FAILURE

This pattern indicates the code passed CI checks but failed SonarCloud's external quality gate. The PR is UNSTABLE but safe to merge with `--admin` flag.

Seen on PRs #930, #935, #937 in backlog-15, blocking autonomous batch processing.

## Solution

### Detection Logic
- `check_pr_status()` now returns `unstable_sonarcloud` status
- Detects when:
  1. "SonarCloud Analysis" check has `conclusion: SUCCESS`
  2. "SonarCloud Code Analysis" check has `conclusion: FAILURE`
  3. No OTHER checks have failures (only SonarCloud external gate failed)

### Merge Logic
- `cmd_pr_lifecycle()` treats `unstable_sonarcloud` same as `ready_to_merge`
- Logs clear message: "SonarCloud external gate failed but GH Action passed - using --admin"
- Stores `sonarcloud_unstable: true` in `triage_result` JSON for audit trail

### Merge Execution
- `merge_task_pr()` checks for `sonarcloud_unstable` flag in two places:
  1. From `triage_result` in DB (set during pr_lifecycle)
  2. From current `check_pr_status()` call (fallback)
- Adds `--admin` flag to `gh pr merge` command when detected

## Testing

- ✅ ShellCheck: No new issues
- ✅ Bash syntax: Valid
- ✅ Logic verified against PR #930 status check data

## Impact

Unblocks autonomous batch processing when SonarCloud external quality gate fails but CI passes. The supervisor can now auto-merge these PRs instead of blocking indefinitely.

title: t229: Retry workers push to existing PR branch instead of closing and recreating
body:
## Summary

- When `create_task_worktree()` is called with `force_fresh=true` during clean-slate retries, it now checks for an existing open PR on the branch and reuses it instead of deleting the branch (which implicitly closes the PR on GitHub)
- The worktree is reset to `origin/main` for fresh code while keeping the same branch, so the existing PR updates in-place with new commits
- The clean-slate reprompt message now tells the worker about the existing PR so it pushes to it instead of creating a new one

## Problem

During clean-slate retries, the supervisor would:
1. Try to squash-merge any existing PR (premature, may fail)
2. Delete the worktree, local branch, AND remote branch
3. Branch deletion implicitly closes any open PR on GitHub
4. Create a fresh branch from main
5. The retry worker creates a NEW PR — losing all review comments, CI history, etc.

## Solution

When an open PR exists and is validated as belonging to the task:
1. Reset the worktree contents to `origin/main` (fresh code, same branch)
2. If no worktree exists, create one on the existing branch and reset it
3. The existing PR stays open with all its review context preserved
4. Falls back to the old delete+recreate behavior only if the reset fails

The reprompt message is also updated to inform the worker about the existing PR, instructing it to push commits to the existing branch rather than creating a new PR.

## Summary

Fixes the asset chain (`chain`) command which was failing due to three issues:

- **Dialog click interception**: Asset thumbnails with video play button or checkbox overlays intercepted clicks. Now uses multiple click strategies (normal → center-click → force) with proper timeout handling.

title: t233: Pre-dispatch model availability check with distinct exit codes
body:
## Summary

- Enhanced `check_model_health()` to propagate distinct exit codes from `model-availability-helper.sh` (0=healthy, 1=unavailable, 2=rate-limited, 3=invalid-key) instead of collapsing all failures to exit 1
- Updated `cmd_dispatch()` and `cmd_reprompt()` to handle distinct codes with specific log messages and appropriate defer/block behavior
- Added missing health check to `dispatch_review_fix_worker()` (previously spawned workers with no availability check at all)
- Added secondary provider check after model resolution in `cmd_dispatch()` to catch cases where the dispatch model's provider differs from the health tier provider

## Problem

9 wasted worker failures from `ambiguous_ai_unavailable` + `backend_quota_error` caused by workers being spawned against unavailable/rate-limited providers. The root cause was `check_model_health()` collapsing exit codes 2 (rate-limited) and 3 (invalid-key) from the availability helper into a single `return 1`, preventing callers from distinguishing transient rate-limits from permanent key failures.

Additionally, `dispatch_review_fix_worker()` had no health check at all, spawning review-fix workers blindly regardless of provider status.

## Changes

| Function | Change |
|----------|--------|
| `check_model_health()` | Propagates exit 2 (rate-limited) and exit 3 (invalid-key) from availability helper; slow-path probe now distinguishes credits/billing (exit 3) from quota (exit 2) from generic errors (exit 1) |
| `cmd_dispatch()` | Handles distinct exit codes with case statement; adds secondary availability check for resolved model's provider when it differs from health tier |
| `cmd_reprompt()` | Handles distinct exit codes with case statement; still returns EX_TEMPFAIL (75) to avoid double-incrementing retry counter |
| `dispatch_review_fix_worker()` | New: pre-dispatch availability check (was completely missing) |

## Testing

- `bash -n` syntax check: PASS
- `shellcheck --severity=warning`: No new warnings (all existing are pre-existing SC2034 unused vars in unrelated functions)
- No functional test changes needed — the exit code propagation is backward-compatible (callers that used `if ! check_model_health` still work since non-zero is still falsy)

title: feat: retry logic, credit guard, and cost estimation for Higgsfield automator (t236.1)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of Higgsfield automator production hardening (t236). Adds three reliability features:

- **Retry with exponential backoff**: `withRetry()` wrapper handles transient failures (network timeouts, page load errors). Non-transient errors (content policy violations, missing assets) are not retried. Video/lipsync operations get max 1 retry due to high credit cost.
- **Credit guard**: Checks cached credit balance before expensive operations. Blocks with clear error message if insufficient credits. Warns when credits are low (<3x estimated cost). Use `--force` to override.
- **Credit cost estimation**: Maps each operation type to approximate credit cost (image:2, video:20, lipsync:10, upscale:2, pipeline:60, etc.). Adjusts for batch size, video duration, and seed bracket range.

## New CLI flags
- `--force` — Override credit guard (proceed even with low credits)
- `--dry-run` — Navigate and configure but don't click Generate (Phase 5 will implement)
- `--no-retry` — Disable automatic retry on failure

## Testing

- `--force` bypasses the guard and proceeds

title: t237: Retroactive PR backfill for supervisor DB
body:
## Summary

- One-time data migration script to backfill `pr_url` for deployed/verified tasks that had `no_pr`/`task_only`/empty values
- Searches all merged PRs on GitHub for branch name or title matches using word-boundary validation (same logic as `validate_pr_belongs_to_task()` from t232)
- Writes `proof_logs` entries for full audit trail of all decisions (linked, no_match, skip_cross_linked)

## Migration Results

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| Tasks processed | 62 |
| PRs linked | 52 |
| No PR found | 9 (8 diagnostic tasks + t031) |
| Proof log entries | 54 |

### Remaining unlinked (expected — no matching merged PRs exist):
- `t031` — no merged PR found on GitHub
- `t071-diag-1`, `t073-diag-1`, `t074-diag-1`, `t075-diag-1`, `t076-diag-1`, `t097-diag-1`, `t100-diag-1`, `t120-diag-1` — diagnostic tasks that never had their own PRs

## Implementation

The script (`migrate-pr-backfill.sh`):
1. Pre-fetches all 712 merged PRs from GitHub into a local cache
2. For each task, uses jq regex with negative lookahead to match task IDs precisely (e.g., `t132` won't match `t132.2`)
3. Validates each candidate via `gh pr view` with word-boundary matching on title and branch
4. Checks for cross-contamination (PR already linked to another task)
5. Updates DB and writes proof log entries with `decision_maker = 'migrate-pr-backfill.sh (t237)'`

Supports `--dry-run`, `--verbose`, and `--task <id>` for testing/re-running.

## Fixes during implementation

- Log output was going to stdout, corrupting JSON pipeline — fixed to use stderr
- Initial run had 9 DB lock timeouts from concurrent supervisor pulse — increased busy_timeout from 5s to 15s, re-ran successfully

title: t236.3: Batch operations — batch-image, batch-video, batch-lipsync with concurrency control
body:
## Summary

- Adds `batch-image`, `batch-video`, `batch-lipsync` commands to the Higgsfield UI automator with configurable concurrency control
- Implements JSON manifest input format (simple prompt arrays or structured jobs with defaults)
- Adds resume capability (`--resume`) with persistent `batch-state.json` for recovering from failures

## Design

**batch-image**: Runs N parallel browser sessions (default concurrency: 2) each generating one image. Uses a generic `runWithConcurrency()` limiter.

**batch-video**: Leverages the existing `submitVideoJobOnPage()` + `pollAndDownloadVideos()` pattern from the pipeline command. Submits jobs in batches of `concurrency` (default: 3), then polls for all results simultaneously. This is optimal because video generation time (4-10 min) dominates over submission time (~30s).

**batch-lipsync**: Sequential by default (concurrency: 1) since lipsync is slower and more resource-intensive. Supports parallel execution when explicitly configured.

**Shared features**:
- Credit guard integration with manifest-aware cost estimation
- Retry with exponential backoff per job (1 retry)
- `batch-state.json` persistence for resume after crashes/timeouts
- Shell wrapper with input validation in `higgsfield-helper.sh`

## Manifest format

```json
// Simple array
["prompt 1", "prompt 2", "prompt 3"]

// Structured with defaults
{
  "jobs": [
    { "prompt": "A sunset over mountains", "model": "soul" },
    { "prompt": "A cyberpunk city", "aspect": "16:9" }
  ],
  "defaults": { "model": "nano_banana", "aspect": "9:16" }
}
```

## Verification

- ShellCheck: zero violations
- Node.js syntax check: passes
- Pattern follows existing `pipeline()` and `seedBracket()` batch patterns

title: fix: add missing local declarations in cmd_transition to prevent cross-contamination
body:
## Summary

- Adds `local` declarations for `session_id`, `worktree`, `branch`, `log_file`, and `pr_url` in `cmd_transition()`
- These 5 variables were assigned in the `case` block without `local`, causing them to leak into the shell's global scope
- When the pulse cycle calls `cmd_transition()` in a loop for multiple tasks, stale values from a previous call would be picked up by `${branch:-}` / `${pr_url:-}` checks and written to unrelated tasks' DB rows

## Root Cause

This was the root cause of **all PR cross-contamination** we've been tracking:
- 6 historical duplicate PR links (PRs #657, #761, #805, #810, #922, #925)
- Ongoing backlog-19 contamination where PR #962 (t236.1) was linked to t236.2-5 and t238
- t236.1's branch column was overwritten from `feature/t236.1` to `feature/t236.5` (the last dispatched task)

## Why t232 didn't catch it

The centralized `link_pr_to_task()` (t232) validates PR ownership when called explicitly. But `cmd_transition()` has its own `--pr-url` flag that writes directly to the DB — and the stale global variable caused it to silently pass a wrong PR URL without going through validation.

## One-line fix

```bash
# Before (line 1695):
local task_id="" new_state="" error_msg=""

# After (lines 1695-1696):
local task_id="" new_state="" error_msg=""
local session_id="" worktree="" branch="" log_file="" pr_url=""
```

## Verification

- ShellCheck passes (no new violations)
- The `local` keyword ensures variables are scoped to the function and reset to empty on each call
- Subsequent calls without `--branch`/`--pr-url` will correctly see empty values and skip the DB update
